artists.biography:
Jean Michel André Jarre (born 24 August 1948 in Lyon) is a French composer, performer and music producer. He is a pioneer in the electronic, ambient and New Age genres, and known as an organiser of outdoor spectacles of his music featuring lights, laser displays, and fireworks.

Jarre was raised in Lyon by his mother and grandparents, and trained on the piano. From an early age he was introduced to a variety of art forms, including those of street performers, jazz musicians, and the artist Pierre Soulages. He played guitar in a band, but his musical style was perhaps most heavily influenced by Pierre Schaeffer, a pioneer of musique concrète at the Groupe de Recherches Musicales.

His first mainstream success was the 1976 album Oxygène. Recorded in a makeshift studio at his home, the album sold an estimated 12 million copies. Oxygène was followed in 1978 by Équinoxe, and in 1979 Jarre performed to a record-breaking audience of more than a million people at the Place de la Concorde, a record he has since broken three times. More albums were to follow, but his 1979 concert served as a blueprint for his future performances around the world. Several of his albums have been released to coincide with large-scale outdoor events, and he is now perhaps as well known as a performer as a musician.

As of 2004 Jarre had sold an estimated 80 million albums. He was the first Western musician to be allowed to perform in the People's Republic of China, and holds the world record for the largest-ever audience at an outdoor event.

perplexity.description:
Oxygène 3 is the nineteenth studio album by French electronic pioneer Jean-Michel Jarre, released in December 2016 on the 40th anniversary of the original Oxygène. Continuing the composer's long engagement with his signature work, the album comprises seven newly composed pieces designated as parts 14 through 20 of the ongoing Oxygène composition. The project emerged during Jarre's work on his Electronica albums, which explored the history and future of electronic music through collaborations with numerous guest artists.

Musically, Oxygène 3 balances contemporary production techniques with the aesthetic principles established by the original 1976 album. While incorporating more uptempo, trance-influenced moments than its predecessor, the album maintains the meditative and atmospheric character that defined the Oxygène series, avoiding overtly modern or trendy production choices. The work demonstrates Jarre's commitment to thematic consistency across decades, using updated technology to expand rather than fundamentally reimagine the sonic world he created four decades earlier.

As a standalone release, Oxygène 3 functions as a substantial continuation of the series rather than a nostalgic reissue. The album represents Jarre's sustained artistic investment in the Oxygène concept, following previous installments including the 1997 sequel Oxygène 7-13 and a remastered version of the original from 2007. Released on Columbia/Sony Music, the album was issued in multiple formats, including a 180-gram clear vinyl edition.
